methods.label: Compare prices per unit of detergent
methods.explanation:
A better buy has a lower price per unit of detergent. Use the amount in a small box as one detergent unit and its price as one price unit. These common choices of units preserve all price and amount comparisons.

The large box contains \(2\) detergent units. The medium contains \(20\%\) less than the large, so its amount is
\[
0.8\cdot2=1.6.
\]
The medium costs \(50\%\) more than the small, giving a price of \(1.5\). The large costs \(30\%\) more than the medium, giving
\[
1.3\cdot1.5=1.95.
\]
Divide each price by its positive detergent amount:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S &: 1\div1=1,\\
M &: 1.5\div1.6=0.9375,\\
L &: 1.95\div2=0.975.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(0.9375<0.975<1\), the order from best to worst buy is \(\boxed{MLS}\), choice E.
